inputs.name: Axe 2004 prevalence
inputs.scope: one beta-lactamase domain, extrapolated to any domain-sized fold

inputs.name: Eden's molecules ever
inputs.cite: claim file D q1 (Day relaying Eden)

day.reading: functional sequences are so rare that random search fails; Taylor says one-step isolation from unbiased libraries is impossible
day.holds: every printed figure reproduces: 1e52 x 1e-77 = 1e-25 expected hits; Taylor's product is 5.04e23 (printed 5 x 10^23), a frequency of 2e-24 among fully randomised 100-mers; Taylor's own conclusion (D11 q4) is the one-step impossibility

critic.reading: the three frequencies are for different proteins, lengths and functions and differ by many orders
critic.holds: Axe 1e-77 to Taylor 2e-24 is 53.3 orders; to Keefe & Szostak's lower bound 6.7e-13 it is 64.8; binding (Keefe & Szostak) is not catalysis (Taylor), and Axe's 1e-77 is a bound extrapolated from one domain; per-sequence prevalence is not connectivity (R4 D1-spike leaves this regime untouched)

notes: Data-check object; no verdict moves. The 53 and 65 orders compare unlike quantities (lengths 80, 100 and domain-sized; binding against catalysis; Axe's figure an 'as low as' bound, Keefe & Szostak's a lower bound on frequency), so they bound the disagreement and do not average to one prevalence. On Axe's per-signature 1e-64 the gap to Taylor is 40.3 orders. Taylor prints both '5 x 10^23' (the product, 5.04e23) and '~10^24' (the summary sentence); both are the same estimate rounded. No Day text in the corpus cites Axe (D10).
